lesson_title: Loans, Hire Purchase and Insurance: the True Price of Pay-Later
hook_text: The advert says R3 499 a month for the car. The contract says R285 900. Both are telling the truth.
clip_script: Every pay-later deal hides its real price, and one sum finds it: add up EVERYTHING you will ever pay. The lounge suite says R11 999. On hire purchase — R1 199,90 deposit, then R589,50 a month for two years — grab the calculator: total R15 347,90. The couch costs R3 348,90 extra, and the store owns it until the last payment. Now the car. R3 499 a month sounds doable — that's the design. Hiding in month sixty: a balloon payment of R56 970, thirty percent of the car, postponed, not forgiven. Deposit plus sixty instalments plus balloon: R285 900 for a R189 900 car. R96 000 extra. Pay it, borrow again, or sell the car to settle it — the bubble always bursts. The loan advert plays the same game: R1 095 a month, but add the service fees and the initiation fee, and R25 000 borrowed costs R18 111,50 in credit. So the rule that beats every advert: never judge a deal by its monthly number. Total everything, compare it with the price, and make the difference say its name out loud.
visual_style: Price tags peeling back to reveal bigger totals underneath; a calculator stacking deposit, instalments and a swelling red balloon that bursts into a R56 970 bill; a contract's total-cost line highlighted while the advertised instalment shrinks.
mood: Streetwise and protective, the voice of someone who reads the whole contract before the salesperson finishes smiling.
pacing: Quick through the couch, a suspenseful build to the balloon reveal, a hard stop on R285 900, then calm and firm through the closing rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never let a monthly payment lie to you again.
